answer: A licensed forge anchors seats to metal mass rather than keys. Each applicant consigns a distinct heat lot: the furnace logs its serial, charge weight, ore from a registered ledge outcrop, and charcoal from a named meadow coppice. Seats issue in proportion to tonnage melted, and a lot retires once its metal backs its quota. Two thousand wallets on one server share one heat-lot trail and collapse into a single seat. Cheating means buying, hauling and assaying real tonnage per lot, a cost that grows linearly while marginal seat yield stays flat.
